transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-10-08 UTC
Start: 15:00 | Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Nguyen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood CSM), Ben Hart (CTO - Oceanic), Maya Singh (Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Sita Rao (Procurement)

Summary:
- Renewal/expansion check-in to discuss upcoming contract renewal in November, interest in increasing committed capacity (dedicated GPUs) and enabling EU + APAC regions, and confirming security/compliance requirements for contract extension.
- Agreed to run a performance benchmark in EU region using Oceanic test set; Redwood to provide updated pricing and draft contract.

Topics:
- Capacity upgrade (4 -> 12 GPUs reserved), burst capacity and autoscale policies
- Regional expansion: EU (Frankfurt) and APAC (Singapore) latency/cost tradeoffs
- Contract term options: 12 vs 24 months, discount tiers, SLA expectations
- Security: SOC 2, KMS/HSM, VPC/private deployment considerations

Transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in, hope you all had a good week. we have about 40 minutes, wanted to run through renewal timeline and expansion asks.
[00:12] Ben: yeah thanks Alyssa. busy week, appreciate you setting this up. so main thing from our side is capacity — we expect Q1 next year load to increase, looking at going from our current 4 GPU reserved pool to roughly 12. and we also need EU region for customers in EMEA.
[00:28] Diego: got it. thanks Ben. are those 12 GPUs expected as steady reserved capacity or do you want some burst window? like 12 guaranteed and then burst to 18 during peaks?
[00:41] Ben: good question. probably a mix; baseline 12, allow bursts to 18 for marketing spikes. cost sensitive, though, so would like recommendations on batching and quantization to keep unit costs in check.
[00:56] Maya: and just to add, we also want APAC coverage — Singapore ideally — because latency for our enterprise retail customers over there is pretty bad. so two regions: EU + APAC.
[01:10] Alyssa: okay makes sense. for renewal timing our records show your current contract term ends 2026-11-30, so we're in that 30-day window. we can propose 12 or 24 month extensions with committed capacity pricing which will materially lower per-token costs.
[01:26] Sita: from procurement, timeline is tight but doable. we need SOC2 docs and a simple statement of work. can you send a draft contract and pricing options by Oct 22?
[01:37] Alyssa: yes we can. action item noted. i will send pricing + a contract stub.
[01:42] [crosstalk]
[01:44] Diego: on the technical side, we recommend pinning model variants for the Dedicated pool — that reduces cold-starts and keeps latency SLOs stable. also we have automatic KV cache and prefix caching but want to confirm how you persist KV cache across region failovers.
[02:01] Liam: quick note — we currently rely on a home-grown cache but we'd prefer Redwood handle more of the KV caching; fewer moving parts for us. is the KV cache multi-region replicated?
[02:12] Diego: currently we have cross-region fallbacks but not active-active KV replication in all setups; for dedicated we can enable region-affinity and warm KV snapshots. i might have said K V cash earlier in an email, sorry for the typo.
[02:25] Maya: lol noted. the important bit is state transfer time — if a region fails over, we don't want long cold-seq penalties.
[02:34] Diego: agreed; our recommended approach is warm snapshots + quick rehydration. for the EU/SG nodes we can pre-warm top prefixes. we'll include details in the benchmark run.
[02:46] Alyssa: benchmarks — Diego, can we propose a 2-hour perf run in Frankfurt using Oceanic test set and your traffic replay?
[02:55] Diego: yes, that's doable. we'll need the traffic profile and seq length distribution, and a sample prompt set. can you send that, Liam?
[03:05] Liam: sure, i'll pull our last 30 days traffic and a small sample of prompts. expect that by Monday.
[03:12] Sita: procurement question — are there export or data residency constraints we need to be aware of for EU? also, what about encryption and KMS?
[03:22] Alyssa: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) in Redwood Private and Dedicated; logs and audit trails can be configured to meet data residency. we'll attach the SOC 2 and KMS integration docs.
[03:34] Ben: is SSO/SAML and RBAC already in place? we need SAML for our enterprise SSO and strict RBAC on model access.
[03:43] Priya: yes, we support SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC in the console. i can send an admin guide.
[03:50] Maya: curious about performance delta between Hosted API and Dedicated. last time you mentioned some kernel-level optimizations and arch-specific improvements. any numbers for 8k seqs?
[04:02] Diego: rough numbers — for a 8k sequence on the Dedicated runtime with optimizations we see ~150ms per token at p95 on A100-equivalent setups; hosted numbers vary since multi-tenant overhead and routing change things. we'll include per-model bench results in the report. there might be slight discrepancies due to quantization choices.
[04:19] Ben: ok, good. on pricing — can you outline what the committed capacity discount tiers are? e.g., 12 GPUs committed for 12 months vs 24 months?
[04:29] Alyssa: yes. for committed GPU pools we typically do: 12-month commit = 10% discount, 24-month commit = 18% discount; larger pools or multi-region commitments get additional concession. i'll send a detailed sheet.
[04:42] Sita: do you offer a blended price if we commit across regions? we might want a combined EU+US commitment.
[04:51] Alyssa: we can do blended pricing, yes; we'll spell out per-region unit economics and an overall blended option.
[04:58] Liam: one constraint — our infra team prefers to keep logs within our VPC for compliance. how fast can Redwood support a Private deployment or VPC peering?
[05:09] Diego: Private deployments take more time — typically 6-8 weeks for on-prem or fully air-gapped. VPC peering or Private control plane with customer-managed networking is quicker; we can do that in 2-3 weeks depending on approvals.
[05:21] Ben: 2-3 weeks is fine if we start now. procurement will need the statement of work and SLA. what SLA do you offer for Dedicated?
[05:30] Alyssa: Dedicated has SLA options up to 99.95% with compensation SLAs in the contract; for stricter enterprise needs we can negotiate.
[05:38] Maya: any fallback story if capacity is exhausted in a region? we can't have customers seeing 5s token latencies if we run out.
[05:46] Diego: we have smart routing policies: fall back to regional compatible model variants or route to burst capacity in a different zone; the tradeoff is slightly higher latency. we also support canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies to keep the app online.
[05:58] Ben: ok good. regarding models: we run a mix of open LLMs and a finetuned variant. can you host custom fine-tuned models in the Dedicated pool?
[06:08] Diego: yes, customers can pin custom models. we recommend packaging them with the runtime optimizations. there's a model onboarding checklist i can share.
[06:15] Priya: i'll send the onboarding guide along with the admin SAML doc and the SOC report.
[06:21] Sita: procurement asks about payment terms — net30? we usually do net45. is that negotiable?
[06:27] Alyssa: we can be flexible for enterprise deals; net45 is possible with contract language.
[06:33] Maya: one more technical ask — how does Redwood handle quantization across regions? we've seen accuracy regressions with aggressive 4-bit quant.
[06:44] Diego: good callout. Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles by workload. for sensitive generation we suggest 8-bit or mixed precision; we'll include a recommended quantization policy and quality regression monitoring tied to prompt sets.
[06:58] Ben: sounds good. can we get a test plan for the benchmark? what will you measure?
[07:05] Diego: we'll measure token latency p50/p95/p99, throughput at target concurrency, cold-start times, and regression on quality metrics using your eval prompts. also memory/KV warmup times for failover scenarios.
[07:19] Liam: i will also add our peak window traffic so you can simulate realistic spikes.
[07:24] Alyssa: great. recap and next steps: i'll send pricing + contract stub by Oct 12 to start legal review, Diego will schedule the EU benchmark and run with the test set (aiming for Oct 15), Liam will share traffic and prompts by Oct 11, and Sita will share procurement timeline and contract template.
[07:42] Sita: yes we'll aim to turn around procurement feedback within a week of receiving the stub.
[07:48] Ben: assuming the benchmark looks good and pricing checks out, we are leaning toward a 24-month commit with blended EU+US capacity and burst to APAC.
[07:58] Priya: noted. i'll prepare the tech docs and send over.
[08:02] Alyssa: any other questions?
[08:05] Maya: one small one — are there any vendor lock-in concerns if we use Redwood Private vs Dedicated? we want portability.
[08:13] Diego: we prioritize portability: model artifacts and prompts are portable, and we document config. Dedicated uses standard containerized runtime; Private on-prem has some extra integrations but we'll provide migration docs.
[08:24] Ben: cool. thanks everyone.
[08:27] Alyssa: thanks folks, we'll follow up with the deliverables.
[08:30] Diego: thanks, bye.

Notes/Attachments referenced:
- Pricing sheet (to be sent)
- SOC 2 Type II report (attached soon)
- KMS/HSM integration guide (attached soon)
- Benchmark plan (to be scheduled Oct 12-15)

End of recording.
